title: Do they arrive together? Round bowl: 3.2 s apart. Curved bowl: 0.000 s apart, every crossing.
description:
Do five balls dropped from five heights reach the bottom together? Two bowls, no friction, the same equation (a bead on a wire, s'' = -g dy/ds, RK4 at 600 steps per second). The round bowl is a circle of radius 0.497 m. The curved bowl is a cycloid of the same depth, 1.561 m wide. The balls start at 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 percent of the depth (0.099 to 0.497 m).

Measured (deterministic, no seed):
- round bowl periods: 1.452, 1.494, 1.543, 1.600 and 1.669 s from release angles of 36.9, 53.1, 66.4, 78.5 and 90.0 degrees; each matches the exact elliptic-integral period
- round bowl: first arrivals 0.363 to 0.417 s, 0.054 s apart; the spread grows every crossing: 1.03 s at crossing 10, 2.12 s at 20, 3.21 s at 30, 4.30 s at 40, 5.17 s at crossing 48
- curved bowl: every ball's period is 2.000 s; first arrival at 0.500 s; spread 0.000 s at all 40 crossings
- energy drift under 1e-10 in both bowls
- the cycloid holds exactly 20 periods in 40 s, so the last frame is the first frame and the video loops; the round-bowl balls are lifted back to their marks over the last 1.2 s

Why: on a cycloid the force along the wire is proportional to the arc distance from the bottom, so the ball is a perfect harmonic oscillator and its period does not depend on where it starts (Huygens' tautochrone, 1673). On a circle the period grows with the amplitude.

The numbers in the narration are the printed outputs of this exact run.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
